name: Fenra Yuzu-Saffron Hard Candy
description: Small, jewel-clear hard candies combining yuzu citrus with saffron — one of the few remaining natural saffron-analog compounds that approaches the real thing at a Tier 3-accessible price point. Sold in small corked glass jars.
flavor_profile: Bright yuzu citrus with a warm, slightly metallic saffron sweetness underneath; long-lasting hard candy that shifts flavor in phases as it dissolves, finishing with a honeyed floral note
cultural_context: The glass jar format and saffron-adjacent flavoring make Fenra Yuzu-Saffron a popular host gift in Tier 3-4 social circles — an affordable way to signal taste and generosity without the extravagance of real-ingredient confections; the jar itself is often kept and repurposed.
story_hooks: Fenra's saffron-analog formula is stolen by a corporate espionage operative, and the small artisan company must decide whether to pursue the theft legally — exposing their proprietary process — or absorb the loss.
A Tier 5 chemist claims Fenra's 'analog' actually contains trace real saffron sourced from an unlicensed urban farm, which would make the product simultaneously more valuable and legally precarious.
The distinctive glass jars are being used to smuggle micro-dosed contraband compounds through Tier 3 social events, and Fenra is completely unaware their product has become a delivery mechanism.
